newsitem.title: FRANCE: ACCOR STOCK RALLIES ON H1 SALES.
newsitem.headline: ACCOR STOCK RALLIES ON H1 SALES.

text.p: Shares in French hotel group Accor were sharply higher on Thursday after the company reported better than expected first-half sales.
Accor said on Wednesday after the bourse close that its sales rose 8.3 percent to 15 billion francs and it reported a 14.3 percent jump in turnover in the hotel business.
Brokers said the sales figures were very good and at least one analyst expected to revise the earnings estimates higher.
The stock was the top gainer on the CAC, climbing 5.16 percent to 999 francs at 0925 GMT.
Even without the beneficial impact of the gains in the dollar and sterling, the hotel business's turnover would have risen by double-digits, chairman Jean-Marc Espalioux said.
He also said in an interview with Reuters that an increase in corporate tax would have only a slight impact on 1997-99 results and he reiterated his forecast for a profit rise this year.
"They were good results, showing a strong growth acceleration in the second quarter," said analyst Baudouin Furge at brokerage CCF Elysees Bourse.
Second-quarter sales rose 9.9 percent -- 6.3 percent on a like for like basis -- after growing 6.4 percent in the first quarter, or 2.8 percent on a like for like basis.

Furge said the figures showed strong growth in Accor's two key businesses -- hotels and vouchers -- and signalled an acceleration in the European hotel business's recovery. The vouchers business, in which Accor is a global leader, was helped by a stabilisation in Brazil's economy.

The analyst, who recently revised his earnings estimates upward, expects Accor to show a rise in profit this year of 30 percent to 1.37 billion francs excluding the gain from the sale of Compass shares.
Another analyst said he thought Espalioux's forecast for a 20 percent rise this year in pre-tax, pre-exceptional profit was extremely conservative.
Brokerage Natexis said the sales figures augur an excellent year and it expects to raise its earnings estimates.
